subject.title: feat(durable): hand off wakes to session queue

question: Should a resolved durable wake be allowed to enqueue a `systemEvent` into the current canonical session after that session key has been reset to a new session ID?
rationale: Source and proof establish exactly-once queue ownership transfer, but repository behavior already distinguishes generation-fenced `agentTurn` continuations from cross-generation `systemEvent` delivery; choosing which contract durable wakes inherit affects stale-context injection, session isolation, and recovery semantics.

options.title: Fence to originating generation
options.body: Persist or resolve the originating session ID and leave the wake pending or failed when the canonical key now points to another generation.

options.title: Allow bounded cross-reset delivery
options.body: Treat durable attention as intentionally surviving resets, constrain and authenticate the payload, document the behavior, and add explicit reset-boundary proof.

options.title: Pause for stack redesign
options.body: Keep both PR5 candidates unmerged until the durable wake owner and session-reset contracts are redesigned together.

recommendation.title: Fence to originating generation
recommendation.body: Persist or resolve the originating session ID and leave the wake pending or failed when the canonical key now points to another generation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Gateway restart, session routing, and delivery semantics represented in recent integrated release work.
